content.text: The redline validated. Submitting the finding.

input.quote: 14. INSURANCE. Throughout the term of this Agreement, Contractor shall maintain workers compensation insurance in the amount required by statute, comprehensive general liability insurance with coverage of at least one million dollars ($1,000,000) and professional errors and omissions insurance for bodily injury, property damage or other losses with coverage of at least one million dollars ($1,000,000), in connection with the provision of Services by Contractor pursuant to the terms of this Agreement.
input.rationale: Contrary to the planner's hint that insurance was absent, § 7 para 14 (p0048) contains an insurance covenant binding the Contractor. It delivers several preferred elements: workers' compensation as required by statute, CGL of USD 1,000,000, professional E&O of USD 1,000,000 (which meets the fallback E&O limb), and certificates of insurance on Company request with notice of material change. However, it contains no cyber/privacy liability coverage at any level. That is material here rather than cosmetic: § 8 (p0038) defines Confidential Information as including Company data and records obtained by Contractor, and § 1(c) (p0007) contemplates Contractor personnel working at Company facilities and accessing Company computer systems. The fallback position requires E&O USD 1M *and* cyber USD 2M; with cyber missing entirely, the clause fails the fallback on a material term for a vendor that processes our data, approaching the walk-away concern. The redline therefore makes the smallest possible edit — inserting a cyber/privacy limb at the preferred USD 5,000,000 where Contractor processes Company data — and leaves the remainder of the bargain untouched. Two sub-elements short of preferred are noted but not flagged: the CGL limb states a per-occurrence figure without the USD 2,000,000 aggregate, and E&O sits at USD 1,000,000 rather than the preferred USD 2,000,000 (expressly acceptable at fallback). The permitted reliance on "self-insurance" is likewise a minor point only. Given the engagement is a task-by-task consulting arrangement performed largely at Contractor's own facility, the comment offers USD 2,000,000 cyber as a sensible fallback landing zone.

proposal.summary: Add cyber/privacy liability coverage to the existing insurance covenant, which currently omits it.
proposal.comment: [Playbook] The insurance covenant covers general liability, E&O and workers' compensation but omits cyber/privacy coverage, so we have added it — the Contractor obtains Company data and records and may access our systems and facilities. Our playbook asks for USD 5,000,000 cyber cover where a vendor processes Company data; we can accept USD 2,000,000 if the engagement scope stays limited.
